subject.title: Long streaming model responses cause event loop starvation

question: Should maintainers require fresh current-main long-output Gateway stress proof before allowing a new fix PR for this streaming-starvation report?
rationale: Current code has shipped mitigations, but the remaining issue boundary depends on whether a real Gateway under long streaming output still starves and which downstream surface is responsible.

options.title: Require stress proof first
options.body: Keep this issue open and keep new fix PRs blocked until a current-main DeepSeek or synthetic long-output run identifies the actual remaining hotspot.

options.title: Sponsor a bounded runtime fix now
options.body: Approve a maintainer-owned fix direction such as stronger cooperative yielding or stream backpressure before fresh proof, accepting the risk of touching the wrong layer.

options.title: Route only to adjacent issues
options.body: Treat channel deadlines, restart recovery, and diagnostic-event work as sufficient owners for now, which would leave the provider-stream starvation report without direct proof or fix ownership.

recommendation.title: Require stress proof first
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and keep new fix PRs blocked until a current-main DeepSeek or synthetic long-output run identifies the actual remaining hotspot.

likelyOwner.reason: Current history points to vincentkoc across the stream mitigation, agent update, Gateway chat projection, and DeepSeek metadata paths most relevant to this decision.
